q: Transition elements are the metals that exist in the block between Groups II and III that is, they are in Groups ____ to 12 of the Periodic Table.
e: Transition elements are the metals that exist in the block between Groups II and III that is, they are in Groups 3 to 12 of the Periodic Table. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The first series 3d transition elements run from scandium ($^{21}Sc$) through ____ ($^{30}Zn$).
e: The first series 3d transition elements run from scandium (21Sc) through zinc (30Zn). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The second series 4d transition elements run from yttrium ($^{39}Y$) through ____ ($^{48}Cd$).
e: The second series 4d transition elements run from yttrium (39Y) through cadmium (48Cd). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The third series 5d transition elements run from lanthanum ($^{57}La$) through ____ ($^{80}Hg$).
e: The third series 5d transition elements run from lanthanum (57La) through mercury (80Hg). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The transition elements are also called the ____ elements because the d orbitals are filled in these elements.
e: The transition elements are also called the d-block elements because the d orbitals are filled in these elements. D-block: transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The first row of the transition elements is in the fourth row (Period ____) of the Periodic Table.
e: The first row of the transition elements is in the fourth row (Period 4) of the Periodic Table. 4: transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: In the 3d series, there are ____ transition elements, namely, scandium (Sc), titanium (Ti), vanadium (V), chromium(Cr), manganese(Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt(Co), nickel(Ni), copper (Cu), and zinc(Zn).
e: In the 3d series, there are 10 transition elements, namely, scandium (Sc), titanium (Ti), vanadium (V), chromium(Cr), manganese(Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt(Co), nickel(Ni), copper (Cu), and zinc(Zn). Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: For the 3d series transition elements, the nuclear charge increases from scandium to copper so that atomic radii show a gradual ____ in their values.
e: For the 3d series transition elements, the nuclear charge increases from scandium to copper so that atomic radii show a gradual decrease in their values. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The decrease in atomic radii occurs because the attraction force between the nucleus and electrons is stronger than the ____ force.
e: The decrease in atomic radii occurs because the attraction force between the nucleus and electrons is stronger than the electron-electron repulsion force. Electron-electron repulsion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: All the transition elements in this series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form ____.
e: All the transition elements in this series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form alloys. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Although the 4s orbital is the outermost orbital, it is slightly ____ in energy than the 3d orbitals.
e: Although the 4s orbital is the outermost orbital, it is slightly lower in energy than the 3d orbitals. Aufbau fills lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy ones.

q: The filling of the 3d orbitals generally obeys ____ rule, with one electron added to each of the five d orbitals before a second electron is added to any one of them.
e: The filling of the 3d orbitals generally obeys Hund's rule, with one electron added to each of the five d orbitals before a second electron is added to any one of them. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: There are two exceptions to the expected regular filling pattern (half-filled or completely filled orbitals); chromium ($^{24}Cr$) and ____ ($^{29}Cu$).
e: There are two exceptions to the expected regular filling pattern (half-filled or completely filled orbitals); chromium (24Cr) and copper (29Cu). The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: In the case of $^{24}Cr$, one electron from the 4s shifts to the 3d orbitals to attain a more stable electronic configuration with the ____ 3d orbitals.
e: In the case of 24Cr, one electron from the 4s shifts to the 3d orbitals to attain a more stable electronic configuration with the half-filled 3d orbitals. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: The electronic configuration of $^{29}Cu$ is [Ar] $4s^1 3d^{10}$, instead of the expected [Ar] $4s^2 3d^9$, because completely filled 3d orbitals have extra ____.
e: The electronic configuration of 29Cu is [Ar] 4s13d10, instead of the expected [Ar] 4s23d9, because completely filled 3d orbitals have extra stability. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: When these metals form ions, the electrons are always removed first from the ____ orbital and then from the 3d orbitals.
e: When these metals form ions, the electrons are always removed first from the 4s orbital and then from the 3d orbitals. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: The electronic configuration of the iron(II) ion ($Fe^{2+}$) is [Ar] ____.
e: The electronic configuration of the iron(II) ion (Fe2+) is [Ar] 3d6. 3d6 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The zinc element has completely filled 3d orbitals and always loses the 2 outer electrons from 4s to give the electronic configuration of [Ar] ____.
e: The zinc element has completely filled 3d orbitals and always loses the 2 outer electrons from 4s to give the electronic configuration of [Ar] 3d10. When these metals form ions, electrons come out of 4s first, then 3d.

q: Completely filled 3d orbitals are so stable that zinc can form compounds in the ____ oxidation state.
e: Completely filled 3d orbitals are so stable that zinc can form compounds in the +2 oxidation state. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: Copper is considered a transition element because the $Cu^{2+}$ ion has incomplete ____ orbitals.
e: Copper is considered a transition element because the Cu2+ ion has incomplete 3d orbitals. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: In a period, the properties of transition elements are very similar in contrast to those of s-block and ____ elements.
e: In a period, the properties of transition elements are very similar in contrast to those of s-block and p-block elements. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: These transition elements have typical metallic properties such as malleability, ductility, metallic lustre, and high ____ strength.
e: These transition elements have typical metallic properties such as malleability, ductility, metallic lustre, and high tensile strength. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: One cubic centimetre ($1 cm^3$) cube of iron is ____ times heavier than a $1 cm^3$ cube of sodium.
e: One cubic centimetre (1cm3) cube of iron is 8 times heavier than a 1cm3 cube of sodium. 8 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Transition elements are significantly less reactive than Group ____ metals.
e: Transition elements are significantly less reactive than Group I metals. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: For example, nickel and copper do not react with water, or catch fire in the air (oxygen), unlike ____.
e: For example, nickel and copper do not react with water, or catch fire in the air (oxygen), unlike sodium. Sodium is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In general, transition metals do not ____ readily in the atmosphere.
e: In general, transition metals do not corrode readily in the atmosphere. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: But ____ is an exception; it rusts easily.
e: But iron is an exception; it rusts easily. Iron is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called ____.
e: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called steel. An alloy is a mixture of metals, often harder or more corrosion-resistant than the pure metal.

q: Most transition elements form ____ compounds, whereas Groups 1 and II metals form white compounds.
e: Most transition elements form coloured compounds, whereas Groups 1 and II metals form white compounds. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Most of them can form ions with different charges, so the transition elements show variable ____ states.
e: Most of them can form ions with different charges, so the transition elements show variable oxidation states. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Most transition elements can form ____ ions.
e: Most transition elements can form complex ions. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Compared to 3d series transition metals, alkali metals have a ____ melting point.
e: Compared to 3d series transition metals, alkali metals have a low melting point. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: Transition elements typically have incompletely filled d orbitals or readily give rise to ions with partially filled ____ orbitals.
e: Transition elements typically have incompletely filled d orbitals or readily give rise to ions with partially filled d orbitals. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The ____ oxidation states are more stable at the beginning of the series, i.e., the left side of Mn.
e: The +3 oxidation states are more stable at the beginning of the series,, the left side of Mn. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Towards the end of the series, i.e., the right side of Mn, ____ oxidation states are more stable.
e: Towards the end of the series,, the right side of Mn, +2 oxidation states are more stable. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The elements in the ____ of the series exhibit more oxidation states than those to the left or right.
e: The elements in the middle of the series exhibit more oxidation states than those to the left or right. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The highest oxidation state is ____ for manganese ($^{25}Mn$).
e: The highest oxidation state is +7 for manganese (25Mn). Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The ions of chromium, manganese, and iron with the highest oxidation states tend to be good ____ agents.
e: The ions of chromium, manganese, and iron with the highest oxidation states tend to be good oxidising agents. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Vanadium and chromium ions with the lowest oxidation state of +2 are good ____ agents.
e: Vanadium and chromium ions with the lowest oxidation state of +2 are good reducing agents. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Transition metals usually have their highest oxidation states in compounds with high ____ elements such as oxygen and fluorine.
e: Transition metals usually have their highest oxidation states in compounds with high electronegative elements such as oxygen and fluorine. Electronegative: transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of incomplete d orbitals or the presence of ____ electrons.
e: The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of incomplete d orbitals or the presence of unpaired electrons. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: The transition metal compounds form coloured ions in an aqueous solution because they absorb part of the visible light and transmit the ____ colour.
e: The transition metal compounds form coloured ions in an aqueous solution because they absorb part of the visible light and transmit the complement colour. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: $Sc^{3+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$ ions are ____ because $Sc^{3+}$ ion has completely empty d orbitals, and $Zn^{2+}$ has completely filled d orbitals.
e: Sc3+ and Zn2+ ions are colourless because Sc3+ ion has completely empty d orbitals, and Zn2+ has completely filled d orbitals. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are unpaired then it is a ____ substance.
e: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are unpaired then it is a paramagnetic substance. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are paired, then it is a ____ substance.
e: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are paired, then it is a diamagnetic substance. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: Substances that are attracted very strongly by the applied magnetic field are said to be ____.
e: Substances that are attracted very strongly by the applied magnetic field are said to be ferromagnetic. Ferromagnetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron, ____, and nickel are ferromagnetic substances.
e: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are ferromagnetic substances. Cobalt is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron is used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia in the ____ process.
e: Iron is used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia in the Haber process. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Vanadium is used in the form of vanadium(V) oxide in the manufacture of sulphuric acid in the ____ process.
e: Vanadium is used in the form of vanadium(V) oxide in the manufacture of sulphuric acid in the Contact process. Contact is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nickel is used as a catalyst in the ____ of alkenes.
e: Nickel is used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of alkenes. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Titanium(IV) chloride ($TiCl_4$) is used for the manufacturing of high-density ____ in industries.
e: Titanium(IV) chloride (TiCl4) is used for the manufacturing of high-density polyethene in industries. Polyethene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A complex ion is an ion, which has a metal ion at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions ____ it.
e: A complex ion is an ion, which has a metal ion at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions surrounding it. A complex ion has a central metal ion bound to ligands through coordinate bonds.

q: A paramagnetic substance is a substance that has unpaired electrons and shows weak attraction towards the external ____ field.
e: A paramagnetic substance is a substance that has unpaired electrons and shows weak attraction towards the external magnetic field. Magnetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A diamagnetic substance is a substance that has no unpaired electrons and shows slight ____ from the external magnetic field.
e: A diamagnetic substance is a substance that has no unpaired electrons and shows slight repulsion from the external magnetic field. Repulsion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A ferromagnetic substance is strongly attracted by the applied magnetic field, and retains its ____ for some time even after the external magnetic field is removed.
e: A ferromagnetic substance is strongly attracted by the applied magnetic field, and retains its magnetisation for some time even after the external magnetic field is removed. Magnetisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Almost all transition metals are good at conducting both heat and ____, making them useful for a variety of applications.
e: Almost all transition metals are good at conducting both heat and electricity, making them useful for a variety of applications. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: Titanium is an integral part of modern construction because it is highly ____, strong, and lightweight.
e: Titanium is an integral part of modern construction because it is highly corrosion-resistant, strong, and lightweight. Corrosion-resistant is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron is usually too ____ to be used as metal alone.
e: Iron is usually too soft to be used as metal alone. Soft is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron is usually mixed with small amounts of other elements to make harder alloy steels with greater ____ strength.
e: Iron is usually mixed with small amounts of other elements to make harder alloy steels with greater tensile strength. An alloy is a mixture of metals, often harder or more corrosion-resistant than the pure metal.

q: Manganese is mainly used in alloys, such as ____.
e: Manganese is mainly used in alloys, such as steel. Steel is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Steel contains about 1% manganese to increase the strength and also improve workability and ____.
e: Steel contains about 1% manganese to increase the strength and also improve workability and resistance. Resistance is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Manganese steel is extremely strong and is used for ____ tracks.
e: Manganese steel is extremely strong and is used for railway tracks. Railway is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Vanadium(V) oxide ($V_2O_5$) is used as a catalyst in the ceramics industry, and as a ____ in the printing and dyeing of fabrics.
e: Vanadium(V) oxide (V2O5) is used as a catalyst in the ceramics industry, and as a mordant in the printing and dyeing of fabrics. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Chromium has many industrial uses due to its toughness and resistance to heat and ____.
e: Chromium has many industrial uses due to its toughness and resistance to heat and corrosion. Corrosion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Chromium is widely used for manufacturing ____ steel.
e: Chromium is widely used for manufacturing stainless steel. Stainless is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Chromium is mainly used in electroplating, tanning, printing, dyeing, catalysts, oxidants, matches, and metal corrosion ____.
e: Chromium is mainly used in electroplating, tanning, printing, dyeing, catalysts, oxidants, matches, and metal corrosion inhibitors. Inhibitors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Manganese is used as a catalyst to reduce the ____ rating in gasoline.
e: Manganese is used as a catalyst to reduce the octane rating in gasoline. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Cobalt ion has brilliant ____ colour used as paint, ink, and pigments.
e: Cobalt ion has brilliant blue colour used as paint, ink, and pigments. Blue is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nickel is used for anti-corrosion coating, and nickel ____.
e: Nickel is used for anti-corrosion coating, and nickel plating. Plating is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Copper is a good conductor of electricity and it is used for electrical wire, circuit boards, water ____, and industrial machinery.
e: Copper is a good conductor of electricity and it is used for electrical wire, circuit boards, water pipes, and industrial machinery. Pipes is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron is used to treat and prevent ____.
e: Iron is used to treat and prevent anemia. Anemia is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Copper has been used to treat Wilson's disease and ____ disease.
e: Copper has been used to treat Wilson's disease and Menkes disease. Menkes is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The surgical instruments are made of transition metals such as stainless steel, cobalt-chrome alloys, ____ and its alloys.
e: The surgical instruments are made of transition metals such as stainless steel, cobalt-chrome alloys, titanium and its alloys. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: Titanium surgical instruments offer several advantages over stainless steel instruments, such as being lightweight, durable, and ____.
e: Titanium surgical instruments offer several advantages over stainless steel instruments, such as being lightweight, durable, and corrosion-resistant. Corrosion-resistant is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Titanium has been used mostly for fabricating dental ____.
e: Titanium has been used mostly for fabricating dental implants. Implants is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
